summary: Defines a Telnet option for checking the round-trip path between two Telnet modules. It is an Internet Standard.

eli5.summary: Like shouting hello into a canyon and timing the echo, this checks that the connection is working and responding.

what is the telnet timing mark option
how does telnet timing mark work
how to flush type ahead in telnet
subtitle: A Telnet option for sending a marker through the data stream to learn that earlier data has been dealt with.

tldr.problem: One end of a Telnet connection sometimes needs to be sure that previously transmitted data has been completely processed, printed, discarded or otherwise disposed of.
tldr.mechanism: The TIMING-MARK option (code 6) sends DO TIMING-MARK, and the other side answers WILL TIMING-MARK at the appropriate place in the data stream, after earlier data.
tldr.outcome: The reply lets the requester measure round-trip delay or decide which buffered input or output to throw away, though the requester must do the discarding itself.

today: RFC 860 is an Internet Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Timing Mark Commands
sections.content:
The option has code 6, but its commands are used a little differently from other options:

  • IAC DO TIMING-MARK: requests that the receiver return a WILL TIMING-MARK at the appropriate place in the data stream.
  • IAC WILL TIMING-MARK: assures the receiver that it is inserted at the appropriate place to synchronize with a DO TIMING-MARK the receiver sent.
  • IAC WON'T TIMING-MARK: refuses to guarantee that.
  • IAC DON'T TIMING-MARK: tells the receiver that a WILL TIMING-MARK it sent was ignored.

By default no explicit attempt is made to synchronize the two ends.
sections.eli5: One side asks 'send me a marker'. The other side puts the marker in line behind everything already waiting and sends it back.

sections.title: Flushing Type-Ahead
sections.content:
The RFC's main example is a full-duplex terminal connected to a full-duplex server that lets the user type ahead while earlier input is processed. When the server hits a command it cannot parse, it would like to discard all the type-ahead, send an error message and resume with what the user types after seeing the error. Input may be buffered in the user's host or elsewhere, so the server sends DO TIMING-MARK and waits for WILL TIMING-MARK.

The appropriate place is just before the first character the user typed after seeing the error. The user can also send WILL TIMING-MARK on his own to mark a point from which his typing should count. The RFC stresses that the system sending DO TIMING-MARK must do the discarding; the reply only helps decide which characters are unwanted. Even a refusal with WON'T TIMING-MARK assures the requester that the refuser has received all previous data.
sections.eli5: If you made a mistake and kept typing, the computer wants to throw away what you typed before you saw the error. The marker shows where the old stuff ends.

sections.title: How the Mark Travels
sections.content:
Process A sends DO TIMING-MARK to B. B can refuse with WON'T TIMING-MARK, or agree by letting the mark flow through its outgoing buffer. Instead of delivering it to the terminal, B enters the mark into its incoming buffer, and when it has passed through, B returns WILL TIMING-MARK to A.

When A receives it, A knows that everything it sent to B before the mark has been delivered, and that everything B sent to A before turning the mark around has been delivered.

The RFC lists three typical uses: measuring round-trip delay to a terminal or another process; resynchronizing after an illegal command by flushing type-ahead; and the dual case, where the terminal user flushes unwanted output from A by sending DO TIMING-MARK and discarding output until WILL TIMING-MARK arrives.
sections.eli5: The marker joins the back of the line, passes through the other computer's waiting lines and comes back. When it returns, the line ahead of it has been cleared.

messages.label: DO TIMING-MARK
messages.note: A asks to synchronize; the mark flows through B's outgoing buffer.

messages.label: WILL TIMING-MARK
messages.note: Sent after the mark has passed through B's incoming buffer.
